scenario: A standard user successfully logs in and then obtains local administrator privileges without authorization before performing a privileged security-related action.
required_evidence: The account initially operates as a standard user.
The account successfully escalates to local administrator privileges.
The privilege escalation is explicitly identified as unauthorized.
A privileged action occurs after the escalation.
The escalation and subsequent privileged action occur on the same host and involve the same user.
forbidden_conclusions: Do not treat the privilege escalation as authorized without evidence of authorization.
Do not ignore the sequence between the privilege escalation and subsequent privileged action.
Do not classify the privilege escalation as benign merely because the initial authentication was legitimate.

scoring_notes.correct_outcome: The system should classify the activity as a confirmed security incident.
scoring_notes.evidence_requirement: The system should connect the initial user state, unauthorized escalation, and subsequent privileged action.
scoring_notes.uncertainty_requirement: High confidence is appropriate because the telemetry explicitly identifies the escalation as unauthorized and shows subsequent privileged activity.
scoring_notes.unsupported_claim_penalty: The system should not dismiss the escalation based solely on the legitimate initial login.
